item.title: lyft bikes
item.description: I’m a frequent user of Lyft Bikes, a.k.a. Baywheels in SF. Some fun facts: If you have a monthly subscription, you pay 29/month.Weirdly,ifyouhavethisfor5months,theywillautomaticallyupgradeyoutotheannualsubscription,whichcosts165, while reducing your charge for the 6th month.

item.title: Deciding if something is on the frontier
item.description: How do you decide if something is on the frontier? I’m a little bit confused. I’ll often want to do analysis which says: take a set of data points, figure out which of the ones are, on the frontier or that are state-of-the-art at the time they are made available, and then plot a trend line so that you can accurately guess what the frontier will be in the future.

item.title: pareto
item.description: I’m a huge fan of the set of concepts named after Vilfredo Pareto. I know nearly nothing about the man himself, but a quick skim of his Wikipedia page suggests that he had some vague visions which were correct, but maybe didn’t quite nail the terminology/definitions himself.

item.title: creating instead of consuming
item.description: Relaxing by creating Chris Lakin had this great post back in the day (archived here) about relaxing by creating instead of by consuming. I haven’t read it in a while, but it still lingers on account of both my bad habit of poor quality relaxation and my related media consumption addiction.

item.description: A number of projects that I’ve started or thought of at some point or another. I don’t care for getting scooped so if you’re interested, please go ahead and do them! Then, do tell me about it so that I can thank you / ask you about how it went.

item.title: fog-of-war chess
item.description: What is Fog of War Chess? Fog-of-war chess is by far, my favorite game in the world. Fog-of-war is a variant of chess (available on chess.com) where you are only able to see the squares your pieces are or where your pieces can move.
